subject: SUM function
notes:
Format read directly from specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.88.2 (line 33495-33499): `FUNCTION SUM ( { argument-1 } … )` — FUNCTION and SUM underlined (required), the argument-list parentheses present, and the braced argument-1 followed by an ellipsis, i.e. ONE OR MORE. Both halves READ and verified. (1) THE REFERENCE SHAPE: CobolExpressions.g4#functionCall `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*`, with SUM present in CobolExpressions.g4#functionName (line 458) — needed because SUM is one of the §8.9 reserved words that is also a §8.11 intrinsic name. The keyword-omitted twin `SUM(…)` rides CobolExpressions.g4#reservedIntrinsicArgFn (`SIGN | SUM`), and IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsic lines 54-63 enforces §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 on it (COBOL1543 unless REPOSITORY declares SUM / FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC) — so the abbreviated form is not accepted unconditionally. Arguments juxtapose or take the §8.3.5 separator via functionArgList. §8.4.3.2.3 SR6 is decided from the DEFINITION before binding (DefinitionPermitsArguments("SUM") is true since MaxArgs > 0), so `FUNCTION SUM (1:4)` draws Sr6ArgumentListError, not a bogus arity error; §8.4.3.3.3 SR2 rejects reference-modifying SUM's numeric result (ResultRefMod, COBOL1629). (2) THE 1..n MULTIPLICITY: IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build line 152 `Add(new("SUM", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "n", "SumScaled", …))` — MinArgs 1, MaxArgs int.MaxValue; IntrinsicBinder.cs line 573 raises COBOL1504 ("takes at least 1 argument(s); 0 given (ISO §15.3)") for `FUNCTION SUM` written with no list or an empty one, and the unbounded max means no upper rejection. The ellipsis also licenses the §15.3 table(ALL) argument: IntrinsicSig.RepeatsAnArgument (MaxArgs == int.MaxValue) gates TryBindAllArgument, and its own diagnostic text names SUM as an example of a `{ argument } …` format. TESTS: tests/WiseOwl.Cobol.Tests.Unit/IntrinsicRepeatedArgumentDriftTests.cs re-reads §15.88.2's `<pre>` block out of specs/ISO_COBOL.md and asserts the catalog's unboundedness EQUALS the presence of the '…' character — spec-derived in the strict sense (the assertion's oracle is the standard's own text, not a hand list). tests/conformance/2023/pb62_all_subscript_runtime_ranges.cob exercises the repeated-argument format over ALL (fixed, ODO, dynamic-capacity, two-level, and a mixed `SUM(F(ALL) WS-E(ALL))`); pb58_argument_predicates_legal.cob exercises the plain 3-argument written form. NOT covered by a dedicated fixture: a zero-argument `FUNCTION SUM` negative case — the COBOL1504 arm was read in source but has no SUM-specific golden; that is a test gap, not a behavior gap (the arm is shared and exercised by other MinArgs rows).

REFUTER (verdict SUSTAINED after independent attack): the format was re-read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33494-33499 and §8.4.3.2.3 re-read whole at :6020ff. SR2 ("If intrinsic-function-name-1 or the ALL phrase is specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph … the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier; otherwise the word FUNCTION is required") and SR6 ("If a function's definition permits arguments and a left parenthesis immediately follows … the left parenthesis is always treated as the left parenthesis of that function's arguments") both check out against IntrinsicBinder.cs:57 (COBOL1543) and :88 (Sr6ArgumentListError, via DefinitionPermitsArguments reading MaxArgs > 0 from the catalog row). The keyword-omitted alternative `reservedIntrinsicArgFn subscriptPart refModPart*` (CobolExpressions.g4:334-346) REQUIRES the subscript group, so a bare `SUM` can never be read as a function reference — which is correct precisely because §15.88.2 has no zero-argument form, and is what keeps the report-writer `SUM OF` clause and the `SIGN` data-description clause from being swallowed. The drift test was read in full and is genuinely spec-derived: it re-scans every `#### 15.x.2 General format` block out of specs/ISO_COBOL.md, keys on the '…' character, asserts a ≥79-row floor on BOTH the spec scan and the catalog scan so the scanner cannot silently find nothing, and asserts the equivalence in both directions — it closes the UNBOUNDED half of `{ argument-1 } …`. The at-least-one half rests on reading only (IntrinsicBinder.cs:573, MinArgs 1) with no SUM-specific fixture, which rule 3 expressly permits for CONFORMS. ONE RESIDUE FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT COUNTED AGAINST THIS ROW: with a runtime-ranged table(ALL) the compile-time count is `all.StaticCount ?? 1` (IntrinsicBinder.cs:572), so an OCCURS DEPENDING object of 0 satisfies MinArgs at compile time and the enumerated list reaches the runtime EMPTY — CobolIntrinsics.Dec.cs#SumDec would then throw IndexOutOfRangeException on `xs[0]` and CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#SumScaled would return 0. §15.3 makes exactly that case undefined ("The evaluation of an ALL subscript shall result in at least one argument, otherwise the result of the reference to the function-identifier is undefined"), so it is not a violation of this format rule; it is worth a robustness note elsewhere, not a downgrade here. Verdict held at CONFORMS.
